5104:
** τοί**, ταί,
_Epic dialect_ and _poetry_ for οἱ or οἵ, αἱ or αἵ, _nominative_ _plural_ of ὁ and ὅ, frequently in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus (_relative_, 8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 3.73, 12.63, more frequently _demonstrative_)}}, not in _Ionic dialect_ Prose, rare in Trag., e.g. {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 424}}: but in _Doric dialect_ and certain other dialects as the Article, Ἱάρων.. καὶ τοὶ Συρακόσιοι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|“SIG” 35 “Ba” (Olympia, 5th c.BC), etc.}}
5107:
** τοιόσδε**, άδε
(_Ionic dialect_ ήδε), όνδε, a form of τοῖος, bearing the same relation to τοιοῦτος as ὅδε to οὗτος, **such as this,** in {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus not so common as τοῖος, but in 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus}} and _Attic dialect_ much more so; sometimes _antecedent_ to οἷος, as ἀοιδοῦ τοιοῦδ᾽ οἷος ὅδ᾽ ἐστί {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 1.371, compare 17.313, 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 24.375: but more frequently _absolutely_, ἀλλ᾽ ὅδ᾽ ἐγὼ τ.}} here am I **such as you see,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 16.205, compare 15.330}}; frequently with implications, **so great, so bad,** etc.; οὔ κε κακοὶ τοιούσδε τέκοιεν {{Refs 8th c.BC+|4.64; τοιόσδε τοσόσδε τε λαός 8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 2.120, 799}}; τοιάδε λαίφεα **such** clothes, i. e. **so bad,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 20.206; τοσόσδε καὶ τοιόσδε 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 2.73: after 8th c.BC: Homerus Epicus antecedent to οἷος, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 576.2, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Meno” 75e, etc.}}; to ὅς, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 7.158}}; rarely to a _conjunction_, as ὡς, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Persae” 179}}: with a qualifying word, τοιόσδ᾽ ἠμὲν δέμας ἠδὲ καὶ ἔργα {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Odyssea Homerus Epicus “Odyssey” 17.313; τοιόσδ᾽ ἐστὶ πόδας 19.359: with the _Article_, ὁ τ. ἀνήρ, αἱ τ. πράξεις, 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Septem contra Thebas” 547, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 895 (Lyric poetry); ἐν τῇ τ. ἀνάγκῃ 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.10; οἱ τοιοίδε 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 330; τὸ τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 358b}}; ἐν τῷ τοιῷδε in **such** circumstances, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.27, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 2.36, etc.: without _Article_, κατὰ τοιόνδε}} in **such** wise, {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.48, 7.10. ; ἕτεροι τ. [prev. author] 1.207; φωνῆς ἐνεχθείσης τοιᾶσδε NT.2Pet.1.17: the sense is made more _indefinite_ by τοιόσδε τις}} **such a** one, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.139, 4.50}}, frequently in _Attic dialect_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Symposium” 173e, +others: in prose narrative τοιάδε}} is, properly, **as follows,** τοιαῦτα **as aforesaid,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.8, +others (compare ὅδε, οὗτος)}}; but this distinction is not strictly observed. _adverb_ τοιῶσδε {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.AD: Adamantius Physiognomonicus “Vent.” 37, 39, 12th c.AD: Eustathius Episcopus Thessalonicensis ad 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta “Prooem.” p.82 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus, etc. [τοῐ- in 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Prometheus Vinctus” 239, “Ag.” 1400, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Oedipus Tyrannus” 435, “Aj.” 453}}; but not so frequently as in τοιοῦτος.]
5112:
Included with: ** τολμ-ηρός**, ά, όν,
usual prose form for τολμήεις, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Antipho Orator 3.3.1, 5th-6th c.BC: Andocides Orator 1.110, 5th c.BC: Lysias Orator 7.19, etc.}}; οἱ-ότατοι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Isocrates Orator 3.21}}; **προθυμία-οτάτη** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.74}}; τὸ τ. τινῶν their **hardihood,** {{Refs|[prev. work] 102}}; τὸ -ότερον your **greater daring,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] 2.87; τ. πολλὰ δρᾶν 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ethica Nicomachea” 1117a2; κἂν εἰ -ότερον εἰρῆσθαι 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Sophista” 267d}}: also in Poets, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Supplices” 305, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Nubes” 445 (_anapaest meter_), 2nd c.BC: Bion Bucolicus 1.60; ἀνοίας οὐδὲν -ότερον 4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 738}}; opposed to εὔτολμος, {{Refs|[prev. author] “Mon.” 153}}. _adverb_ **-ρῶς**{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 3.74, 83, 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Symposium” 2.12, etc.}}: _comparative_ **-ότερον**{{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.126, 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 1.17.7, NT.Rom.15.15}}: _superlative_ τολμ-ότατα {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 3.136.}}
5113:
** τολμ-ητής**, οῦ, ὁ,
**bold, venturous man,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 1.70, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 2.72, 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 20.9.1, 4th c.AD: Adamantius Physiognomonicus 2.5; θυμὸς τ. “Anthologia Graeca” 9.678.}}
5116:
** τόπαζος**, ὁ,
a gem of green hue {{Refs 1st c.AD+|(1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor “Historia Naturalis” 37.107)}}, hence probably **chrysolite** or **peridot,** {{Refs 1st c.AD+|Anthologia Graeca 6.329 (Leon. 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor), 1st c.AD: Josephus Historicus “Antiquitates Judaicae” 3.7.5, 2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta 1121, 5th-6th c.AD: Orphica “Lithica” 278}}:—also **τόπαζον**, τό, Eust.ad {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Dionysius Periegeta [same place]}}; **τοπάζιον**, {{LXX+1st c.BC+|LXX.Exo.28.17, LXX.Psa.118(119).127, 1st c.BC-1st c.AD: Strabo Geographus 16.4.6, 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 3.39, NT.Rev.21.20:—Pliny (“HN” [same place])}} gives the name of **topazon** (variant **topazium**) to two varieties. (From the Trogodyte language _accusative_ to {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st c.AD: Plinius Rerum Naturalium Scriptor}} [same place]; perhaps the same as ταβάσιος.)
5123:
** τουτέστι**,
={τοῦτ᾽ ἔστι}, **that is to say,** {{NT+1st c.AD+|NT.Mark.7.2, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.64c, 7th c.AD: Hephaestio Grammaticus 12.1, 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Syntaxi;” 29.13, “Codex Justinianus [4th-6th c.AD]” 1.1.5.3, etc.}}; _falsa lectio_ in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Fragmenta” 94 (codices SM 5th c.AD: Stobaeus, Joannes).}}
5135:
** τραυμᾰτ-ίζω**,
_Ionic dialect_ **τρωμ-**: _perfect_ τετραυμάτικα Decrees cited in {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 18. 155:}} —_passive_ τετραυμάτισμαι (see. below): _aorist_ _passive_ ἐτραυματίσθην {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Fragmenta” 705}}:— **wound,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.59, +others, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Bacchae” 763, “PPetr.” 3p.59 (3rd c.BC), “BGU” 1780.11 (1st c.BC), NT.Luke.20.12, etc.}}:—_passive_, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 9.61, +others, 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.35, etc.; τετραυματισμένον γὰρ ὡς κύων νεβρὸν.. ἐκμαστεύομεν 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Eumenides” 246; τραυματισθεὶς τολλά 5th c.BC: Thucydides Historicus 4.12.}}

5140:
** τρεῖς**, οἱ, αἱ, τρία, τά:
_genitive_ τριῶν: _dative_ τρισί, also τριοῖσι {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Hipponax Iambographus 51, and τρίεσσι “Delph.” 3(5).80.21 (4th c.BC)}}; _Aeolic dialect_ τρίσσι {{Refs|“Inscription Perg.” 245 B 18 (from Pitana): _accusative_ τρεῖς}} (written τρες {{Refs|“IG” 12.24.16, 44.15, 188.37, 1085, +others), τρία}}: _Doric dialect_ _nominative_ τρέες {{Refs|“Leg.Gort.” 9.48; τρῆς “IG” 12(3).1640 (from Thera)}}; τρῖς {{Refs 4th c.BC+|“SIG” 236 A 10 (Delph., 4th c.BC), “Tab.Heracl.” 1.23; _accusative_ τρίινς “Leg.Gort.” 5.54, +others (for Τρίνς, lengthened to correspond with the other cases)}}; τρῖς {{Refs 6th c.BC+|“IG” 12.838,839 (6th c.BC), “SIG” 239 D ii 28 (Delph., 4th c.BC), “Berl.Sitzb.” 1927.158 (from Cyrene)}}:—**three,** {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 15.187, etc.}}; τρία ἔπεα **three** words, proverbial in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.48}}—for from the earliest times **three** was a sacred and lucky number, especially with the Pythagoreans (compare τριάς), {{Refs 5th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Caelo” 268a11; so τῶν τριῶν μίαν λαβεῖν εὔσοιαν 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 122}}; εἰ καὶ τῶν τριῶν ἓν οἴσομαι{{Refs|[prev. work] 908; compare σωτήρ 1.2:}} —διὰ τριῶν ἀπόλλυμαι I am **thrice,** i. e. **utterly,** undone, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 434 (compare τριάζω)}}; ἡ διὰ τριῶν ἀγωγή the 'trivium', {{Refs 6th c.AD+|6th c.AD: Simplicius Philosophus “in Aristotelis Physica commentaria - Comm. in Arist. Graeca” 1171.34; ἵνα δήσῃ τρία τρία}}**by threes,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|POxy. 121.19 (3rd c.AD). (I.- 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus}} stem **tr[icaron]-,** fuller form **trey-,** _nominative_ **tréy-es** (Sanskrit _tráyas,_ Latin _tres_), whence τρέες, _contraction_ τρῆς and τρεῖς (written τρες {{Refs|“IG” 12.295.11)}}; _accusative_ **tri-ns** (Gothic _prins,_ Sanskrit _tr[imacracute]n_), whence τρῖς and τρίιν; in Gr. the _nominative_ τρεῖς functions as _accusative_ (as in _Attic dialect_), or the _accusative_ τρῖς as _nominative_ ([same places]).)
5148:
** τρῐετ-ία**, ἡ,
**period of three years,** {{Refs 4th c.BC+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “C. Gracchus” 2; κατὰ τ. 4th-3rd c.BC: Theophrastus Philosophus “de Causis Plantarum” 1.20.4, argument ii 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 22, compare 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus 1 “Prooem.” 8, “PAmh.” 2.1c o. 7 (2nd-3rd c.AD), etc.}}; ἐς τ. {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Alex.” 41.}}
5151:
** τρίς**,
_adverb_ of τρεῖς (which see), **thrice, three times,** τ. τόσσα **thrice** as much or many, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 1.213, compare 5.136; δὶς καὶ τ. 6th c.BC: Theognis Elegiacus 633, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Ajax” 433, etc.; δὶς ἢ τ. 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1181 (troch.); τ. τετράκι τε 5th c.BC: Pindarus Lyricus “N.” 7.104; ἐς τ.}}**thrice,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|[prev. author] “O.” 2.68, 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 1.86, 5.105, “GDI” iv p.884 (Erythrae, 4th c.BC), 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 1.25, 2.43; ἐπὶ τρίς}}**thrice,** {{NT+4th c.BC+|NT.Acts.10.16, 11.10, 1st c.AD: Dioscorides (Dioscurides) Medicus “Eup.” 2.19; frequently used merely to intensify the notion, τ. λελουμένη 4th c.BC: Eubulus Comicus 102, etc.}}; especially in compounds, such as τρισάθλιος, τρίσμακαρ, etc., compare τρι-, τριάζω, τρικυμί; but such words may sometimes be written divisim, τρὶς ἄθλιος, etc.: proverbial, τ. ἓξ βαλεῖν throw **thrice** six (the highest throw, there being three dice), {{Refs 8th c.BC+|4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Agamemnon” 33, compare 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Leges” 968e; τρὶς ἓξ νικητήριος βόλος “App. Prov.” 4.99; ἢ τ. ἓξ ἢ τρεῖς κύβοι 5th c.BC: Pherecrates Comicus 124. [ῐ: in 8th-7th c.BC: Hesiodus Epicus “Opera et Dies” 173}} long by position before (ϝ) έτεος.] (I.-{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus}} **tris,** cf. Sanskrit _tris,_ Latin _ter._)
5155:
** τρῐχ-ῐνος**, η, ον,
**of hair,** περικαλύμματα {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Politicus” 279e, compare 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 7.208; χιτῶνες 5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Anabasis” 4.8.3}}; σάκκοι, σάκκος, {{NT+3rd c.BC+|“PSI” 4.427.3 (3rd c.BC), “PTeb.” 796.10 (2nd c.BC), NT.Rev.6.12, 2nd c.AD: Soranus Medicus 2.85, “PGoodsp.Cair.” 30 xxxix 15 (2nd c.AD)}}; ἱδρῷα {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“BGU” 1515 (3rd c.BC)}}; ῥάκη {{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.42.}}
5159:
** τροποφορέω**,
with _accusative_, **bear with another's moods,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|Scholia 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 1479, 10th c.AD: Suidas Legal icographus s. vv. σκύμνος et οὐ χρ; τὸν τῦφόν μου 1st c.BC: Cicero, M. Tullius Orator et Philosophus “Epistulae ad Atticum” 13.29.1}}; variant for{τροφο-} in {{LXX+NT|LXX.Deu.1.31, NT.Act.13.18.}}
5167:
** τρῡγών**, όνος, ἡ,
(τρύζω) **turtle-dove, Columba turtur,** {{NT+5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Aves” 302 (troch.), 979 (hexameters), NT.Luke.2.24, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 6.700, etc.}}; περιστεραὶ τρυγόνες Aristeas 145: proverbial of a great talker, τρυγόνος λαλίστερος {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th-3rd c.BC: Menander Comicus 416, compare 2nd c.AD: Alexander Rhetor 92.3, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 15.88, 4th c.AD: Alciphro Epistolographus 3.29}}; πονηρὰ κατὰ τρυγόνα ψάλλεις, ἐπὶ τῶν ἐπιπόνως ζώντων, [{{Refs 4th c.AD+|4th-5th c.AD: Diogenianus Paroemiographus 7.71, compare 5th c.AD(?): Hesychius Legal icographus see at {τρυγονοψάλλειν}.}}]
**II** a kind of fish, the **sting-ray,** τρυγόνες ὀπισθόκεντροι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Epicharmus Comicus 66, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 489b31, 4th c.BC: Antiphanes Comicus 26.23, 1st c.AD: Celsus Medicus 6.9.6, 2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus Vict. _Attic dialect_ 8}}; compare τρυγόνιος.
**III** an oviparous quadruped of uncertain kind, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Historia Animalium” 540a31.}}
5168:
** τρῡμᾰλ-ιά**, ἡ,
={τρύμη}, **hole,** {{LXX+3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC: Sotades Lyricus 1 (obscene meaning), LXX.Jer.13.4, +others}}; ἡ τ. τῆς ῥαφίδος the **eye** of the needle, {{NT|NT.Mark.10.25}}; βελόνης{{Refs 5th c.BC+|Maria cited in Zos.Alch. p.238 5th c.BC: Bacchylides Lyricus}}; **mesh,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-4th c.BC: Aesopus Fabularum Scriptor 26.}}
5169:
** τρῡπ-ημα**, ατος, τό,
**that which is bored, a hole,** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Eupolis Comicus 354}}; in the ψῆφος, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Ἀθηναίων Πολιτεία” 69.1}}; τ. νεώς, i. e. one of the holes through which the oars worked, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Pax” 1234}}; in the flute, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Archytas Tarentinus Philosophus 1, 1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus 2.389d}}; in a gate-fastening, the hole for the βάλανος, Aen. Tact. 18.3; ῥαφίδος (compare τρυμαλιά) {{NT+5th c.BC+|NT.Matt.19.24; μυρμήκων “Anthologia Graeca” 11.78 (1st c.AD: Lucillius Epigrammaticus); obscene meaning, 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ecclesiazusae” 624, 2nd c.AD: Hermogenes Rhetor “περὶ ἰδεῶν” 2.3, 6th c.AD: Procopius Caesariensis Historicus “Historia Arcana” 9.}}
